newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia has lower trade deficit in January.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia has lower trade deficit in January.

text.p: Tunisia's trade deficit fell to 99.6 million dinars in January 1997 from 170.8 million dinars a year earlier, the National Institute of Statistics said on Friday.
Exports rose 13.3 percent year on year to 475.7 million dinars and imports declined by 2.6 percent to 575.3 million dinars.
Food exports, including olive oil, rose by 79.7 percent to 43.3 million dinars.
Higher prices on the international markets increased energy exports value by 40.7 percent to 45.6 million dinars.
But exports of textiles, Tunisia's first manufacturing earner of foreign currency, grew only by 5.2 percent year on year to 218.3 million dinars.
Exports of phosphates and mining products fell 11.9 percent to 43.6 million dinars.
In full 1996, Tunisia's trade deficit stood at 2.17 billion dinars, down from 2.29 billion dinars in 1995.

Exports amounted 5.372 billion dinars, up by 3.8 percent compared to 5.173 billion dinars in 1995, and imports were worth 7.543 billion dinars, up 1.1 percent compared to 7.464 billion dinars. ($=1.07 dinar)
